thread.title: Brand Rankings Give Two Different Views of Apple, Google

author: Jon Swartz
title: Brand Rankings Give Two Different Views of Apple, Google
text:
What's in a ranking of brands? It depends on whom you poll.
Apple's iPhone X. Illustration: Tiernan Ray for Barron's For Apple (AAPL), it means the difference between No. 1 in one poll ( MBLM Brand Intimacy Report ) and No. 29 in another ( Harris Poll Reputation Quotient ).
Apple ranked first in MBLM's study of brands, based on emotions, for the third straight year. It spoke with 6,000 consumers in the U.S., Mexico, and the United Arab Emirates last year.
Apple stirred personal feelings of "stylish," "modern" and "cool," according to MBLM. Amazon.com (AMZN) was second, followed by BMW (BMW.Germany), Jeep, Walt Disney (DIS), Alphabet's (GOOGL) YouTube, Target (TGT), Netflix (NFLX), Amazon's Whole Foods Market, and Alphabet's Google.
Harris' poll tells quite another story.
Apple and Google both dropped out of the top 10, reflecting growing sentiment among thousands of consumers polled that they have not introduced as many eye-catching products as they have in past years, such as Google Docs, the iPhone, and the iPad, Harris Poll CCO John Gerzema told Reuters.
Apple tumbled to No. 29 after finishing fifth in 2017 and second in 2016. Google dropped to 28th this year from eighth last year.
Amazon was No. 1 for the third straight year in the Harris poll, which surveyed 25,800 adults from Dec. 11 to Jan. 12. Wegmans Food Markets was second, and auto maker Tesla (TSLA) came in third.
Facebook (FB), whose reputation has been battered by questions over its role in Russian efforts to influence the 2016 presidential election, improved to No. 51 in the Harris poll—its best showing since 2014, when it finished 38th.
